assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy link basic peptide hormone biology to a major therapeutic advance in type 2 diabetes and obesity, with growing evidence of cardiovascular and renal benefit. The work is original, clear and of very large clinical and public-health impact. As a neurologist I also note the appetite-regulating central actions, but I judge it on the general criteria.
assessment.attribution: Holst established the physiology of GLP-1 and its secretion, Drucker defined the biology of the receptor, GLP-1 actions and the enteroendocrine axis, and Mojsov contributed the identification of the biologically active truncated peptide and its synthesis. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is a major figure in drug development, but a basic-science-focused trio seems the most defensible. Credit is contested, and other early contributors such as Joel Habener are not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: multiple approved drugs, large randomized outcome trials and a decade-plus of confirmation. Recognition is timely, arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between peptide identification, physiology and drug development is contested.
Whether drug development (Knudsen) should displace one of the basic-science names is unresolved.
I have not independently verified priority claims about the active peptide fragment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology precise, cell-type-specific, millisecond control of activity and transformed the causal study of circuits and behaviour across systems. The conceptual and technical originality is high, and impact on basic research is enormous.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization by Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann, and the demonstration of neuronal use by Boyden and Deisseroth (with Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted photo-activation), make this a compound invention. A three-person prize cannot cover everyone, and which of Deisseroth, Boyden or Miesenböck belongs beside the channelrhodopsin discoverers is a genuine dilemma.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool, widely replicated for 15 or more years. Clinical translation is so far limited, notably in retinal restoration, which tempers but does not remove the case.
uncertainties: Crowded and disputed credit; any three-person selection omits major contributors.
Therapeutic impact is still emerging.
Priority among early neuronal light-activation work is not something I can verify here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of cellular medicine. The discovery-to-patient path is clear, with large impact in hematologic oncology.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed CAR design including co-stimulation and the conceptual framework, June led the pivotal clinical translation in leukemia, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cell trials. Eshhar, Kuwana and others fall outside the supplied names, so a fair configuration is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and long follow-up, though solid-tumor efficacy, toxicity and manufacturing remain limits. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR credit beyond the supplied names (e.g. the original chimeric receptor concept) may be missed.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors.
Rosenberg's contribution is adoptive cell therapy broadly and may be seen as distinct from CAR design.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling logic from the ER to the nucleus with relevance to secretory disease, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. It is an original, clean and conceptually elegant discovery with lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently defined the pathway, with Ire1 and Hac1/XBP1 splicing as the core mechanism. A two-person attribution is clear and compact; Walter's integrated stress response work is partly separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of confirmation and conserved mechanism in mammals. Clinical translation is still developing, which is acceptable for a basic-mechanism prize.
uncertainties: Whether others deserving credit for mammalian UPR branches (e.g. Ron, Kaufman) are excluded.
Direct therapeutic output is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition turned CML into a manageable chronic disease and established the paradigm of targeted kinase inhibitor therapy. It has clear originality and dramatic clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical translation), Lydon (compound development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a plausible trio. Credit for the underlying BCR-ABL and Philadelphia chromosome discoveries (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) lies outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with 20+ years of survival data, though the field may already be seen as recognized through upstream oncogene prizes.
uncertainties: Upstream discoveries are already recognized or unlisted, which complicates the prize framing.
Whether Sawyers' work is a distinct enough contribution compared with the original imatinib development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing yielded nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, a disease previously fatal in infancy. It is a clear mechanism-to-medicine story with large impact on neuromuscular disease and a model for RNA therapeutics.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's splicing-regulatory insight and Bennett's antisense chemistry and development provide a natural two-person configuration. Adrian Krainer and Bennett worked with others (e.g. Hua, Rigo) not on the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016, with several years of real-world data; recognition is reasonably timely but possibly slightly early relative to the long-term evidence.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recognition of other RNA-based medicine awards.
Long-term outcome durability still accumulating.
Contribution of other members of the team may be undercounted.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lgr5 stem cell identification and adult-stem-cell-derived organoids opened a new experimental platform for tissue biology, disease modelling and personalized medicine. It is an original and widely adopted advance.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 and organoid work, with Sato the principal first-author contributor to intestinal organoid culture. Allocation between stem-cell identity and organoid culture could be separated, and others such as Sasai or Barker may be relevant but are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and adopted, but clinical impact is early-stage and the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Clinical translation is not yet demonstrated at scale.
Credit between Lgr5 stem-cell discovery and the organoid method is partly compound.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 control of apoptosis explains cell-survival regulation in cancer and led to BH3 mimetic therapy such as venetoclax, a clear mechanism-to-therapy path with broad biological reach.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams defined the BCL-2 family and its roles in lymphoma, and Vaux showed the survival function; Strasser is a later contributor. Credit with Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto, Cleary and others, outside the supplied list, is a real concern.
assessment.maturity: Mature with an approved drug class, though apoptosis was already honoured in 2002 which may reduce the sense of novelty.
uncertainties: Credit for the original BCL-2 translocation work is shared with unlisted people.
Prior apoptosis prize may count against this.
